text: In the spring of the year one hundred and sixty-one, the old emperor Antoninus Pius lay dying in his country house at Lorium. He had ruled Rome calmly for twenty-three years. According to a later account, when the officer of the guard came to ask for the night's watchword, Antoninus gave him a single word. Aequanimitas. Equanimity. Calmness of mind. Then he turned over, as if to sleep. The young man who learned most from him was his adopted son, Marcus Aurelius, who later wrote that Antoninus did everything as if he had plenty of time.
